records.title: Toward AI‑Driven IoT Cybersecurity: A Preprocessing Framework for Benchmark Datasets
records.abstract: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) systems, found in environments such as smart homes, poses growing cybersecurity challenges. In response, research has examined the role of artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning, in enhancing IoT security. To support this effort, machine learning models have been developed and evaluated on benchmark datasets. However, preparing datasets for machine learning requires preprocessing techniques that are tailored to the specific characteristics of the data. In this context, exploratory data analysis provides insights into dataset structure and distribution, thereby supporting informed preprocessing decisions prior to modeling. Accordingly, this study introduces a reproducible five‑step preprocessing framework for IoT cybersecurity datasets and demonstrates its application to the NF‑ToN‑IoT V1 dataset. The proposed framework is organized into two phases: an exploratory data analysis phase consisting of (1) dataset overview and identification of categorical and numerical features, (2) analysis of missing and zero values, (3) assessment of categorical feature distributions, and (4) assessment of numerical feature distributions; and a preprocessing phase consisting of (5) proportional stratified random downsampling to produce a reduced dataset that preserves the original class distribution. By establishing a systematic, data-driven framework, this study contributes to the preparation of structured datasets for attack detection in IoT environments, with potential applications in smart homes.

records.title: IA vs AI – London Five-Star Hotel Quality Benchmark
records.abstract: <jats:p>Can paid consumer AI services identify the eligible five-star hotels in Greater London and rank the Top 25 using guest-review evidence from one specified year? IA vs AI compared five independent runs each of ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Perplexity (20 primary runs), plus one separate, context-informed ChatGPT run, with a HotScore benchmark locked before AI testing. The original benchmark contained 167 eligible hotels and 148,167 verified guest reviews from five platforms. A later audit identified four additional eligible hotels missing from the locked reference, giving a corrected count of 171 without changing the original file. Claude presented five ranked Top 25 lists and Gemini three. ChatGPT's fifth primary run presented an alphabetical 25-hotel candidate list, not a ranked Top 25; the other primary ChatGPT and Perplexity runs likewise did not deliver a ranked Top 25. Gemini's three ranked lists shared 8, 9 and 7 hotels respectively with the locked HotScore Top 25. Across the 20 primary responses, 24 of the locked HotScore Top 25 hotels were named at least once; the separate informed ChatGPT response named the remaining hotel. This aggregate identification is not a reproduced ranking. The outputs that ranked hotels did not demonstrate a complete and consistently applied five-platform assessment restricted to&nbsp;<code>31 July 2025–31 July 2026</code>. Six distinct ineligible AI candidates were identified in the examined outputs, appearing 15 times. The findings concern these particular consumer services, prompts and recorded settings, not every possible AI workflow. They show that an answer that looks complete is not necessarily a verified annual market ranking, while also showing how AI can help find gaps in a specialist database. AI assistance disclosure. OpenAI ChatGPT supported protocol drafting, text preparation, data organisation and analysis under author review. The author retained responsibility for the study design, source records, benchmark, eligibility decisions and publication&nbsp;</jats:p>

records.title: A Benchmark and Evaluation Framework for Autonomous Context-Aware Data Quality Assessment
records.abstract: <jats:p>Purpose: This study evaluates whether LLM-based and agentic systems can autonomously interpret dataset context and generate context-aware data quality validation rules. Methods: A benchmark was conducted across ten language models, seven prompting or agentic strategies, and three datasets from finance, healthcare, and environmental monitoring, resulting in 1050 executions across 210 model-dataset-strategy configurations. The evaluation framework measured contextual interpretation quality, validation-rule reliability, reference coverage, structural validity, static execution-readiness, hallucination behavior, robustness, efficiency, failure behavior, and ranking confidence. Results: The strongest models achieved moderate semantic performance but limited reference coverage. Few-shot prompting produced the strongest and most stable strategy-level performance, while the evaluated LLM-only multi-agent workflows increased latency, token consumption, API-call exposure, and failures without clear aggregate gains. Structurally valid outputs were not always statically execution-ready, and hallucination behavior varied substantially across models. Conclusion: Current LLM-based systems can support validation-rule discovery and drafting, but generated rules should be treated as candidate artifacts requiring deterministic validation, hallucination auditing, traceability, and human review before operational deployment.</jats:p>

records.title: AI-Driven Spatiotemporal Forecasting Framework for Urban Air Quality Optimization in Smart Cities
records.abstract: This study proposes a robust artificial intelligence–driven framework for forecasting urban air quality using a multi-source dataset integrating pollutant, meteorological, mobility, and energy features across five major Chinese cities. Moving beyond conventional pollutant-only approaches, we introduce a deep hybrid CNN-LSTM architecture capable of capturing complex spatiotemporal patterns in AQI dynamics. The model does much better than traditional methods, with a minimum MAE of 6.3 and a R² of up to 0.89. One of the most interesting things about this is that it includes human-centered indicators, such as the number of people using public transportation and the number of people moving around. These were found to be major factors in permutation importance and SHAP analysis. The model also holds up well under sensitivity testing, especially when PM2.5 and humidity change by ± 10%. The framework uses explainable AI tools to make things easier to understand, which helps policymakers find the most important factors and plan targeted actions. Our method combines statistical accuracy, real-time relevance, and the ability to be used on a large scale. This will lead to smarter, more responsive, and more sustainable air quality management systems in smart cities.

records.title: ConVision Benchmark: A Contemporary Framework to Benchmark CNN and ViT Models
records.abstract: <jats:p>Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) have shown remarkable performance in computer vision tasks, including object detection and image recognition. These models have evolved significantly in architecture, efficiency, and versatility. Concurrently, deep-learning frameworks have diversified, with versions that often complicate reproducibility and unified benchmarking. We propose ConVision Benchmark, a comprehensive framework in PyTorch, to standardize the implementation and evaluation of state-of-the-art CNN and ViT models. This framework addresses common challenges such as version mismatches and inconsistent validation metrics. As a proof of concept, we performed an extensive benchmark analysis on a COVID-19 dataset, encompassing nearly 200 CNN and ViT models in which DenseNet-161 and MaxViT-Tiny achieved exceptional accuracy with a peak performance of around 95%. Although we primarily used the COVID-19 dataset for image classification, the framework is adaptable to a variety of datasets, enhancing its applicability across different domains. Our methodology includes rigorous performance evaluations, highlighting metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and computational efficiency (FLOPs, MACs, CPU, and GPU latency). The ConVision Benchmark facilitates a comprehensive understanding of model efficacy, aiding researchers in deploying high-performance models for diverse applications.</jats:p>

records.title: A Reproducible Quality-Assurance Benchmark for Detecting Contextual Carryover in Biomedical Long-Context AI Assistants
records.abstract: <jats:p>Background and Objective:Long-context large language model (LLM) assistants are increasingly used for biomedical research planning. A practical reliability risk is contextual carryover: obsolete entities or constraints from a previous task may contaminate a new experimental request after a deliberate topic switch. This study introduces a reproducible quality-assurance benchmark and analysis program for detecting contextual carryover in biomedical long-context AI assistants.Methods:The benchmark contains 1,600 matched synthetic biomedical task-switch prompts covering disease models, cell types, assays or omics modalities, candidate drugs, pathways, experimental goals, and safety or ethics constraints. The evaluation program combines sparse residual-stream diagnostics, risk-enriched stress testing, balanced non-enriched checks, same-backend counterfactual controls, direct-parent sensitivity analysis, auxiliary multi-model behavioral coverage, a deployment-oriented dry-run case study, and expert calibration. Two independent biomedical experts with more than ten years of domain experience annotated validation subsets, with adjudication by a senior experimental researcher with more than fifteen years of experience. Automated labels were produced by a fixed Qwen judge rubric and calibrated against expert labels.Results:Representation diagnostics showed that OpenBioLLM had stronger input-proximal old-entity anchoring but lower middle/late old-entity alignment and greater boundary separation than the general comparator. In same-backend counterfactual controls, OpenBioLLM showed a stronger original-A-specific obsolete-entity signal than Llama-3.1-70B (13.5% vs. 3.0%; Fisher&apos;s exact p = 0.000181). In a direct Llama-3 sensitivity subset (n = 382), aggregate semantic carryover was comparable between Llama-3 and OpenBioLLM (15.7% vs. 14.4%; paired difference -1.3 percentage points; bootstrap 95% CI -5.8 to 3.4; McNemar p = 0.653), but category-specific vulnerability differed. Balanced expert validation showed that the automated judge achieved 76.9% precision, 100.0% recall, 98.9% specificity, and 87.0% F1 against strict agreed human carryover labels. A 30-case deployment-oriented dry run showed no baseline carryover under the tested Llama-3.1 route (0/30) but detected one safety-context residue under a QA-intervention prompt (1/30), illustrating how the workflow can audit both assistant behavior and guardrail prompts before release.Conclusions:Contextual carryover is a measurable task-switching reliability risk in biomedical LLM assistants. The proposed benchmark is best interpreted as a reproducible quality-assurance program, regression test, and guardrail-prompt audit rather than a model leaderboard or a real-world prevalence estimator.</jats:p>

records.title: Forced Verdict Gates, Not Graph Sophistication: A Multi-Framework Benchmark of AI Audit Judgement on Real-World Scandal Cases
records.abstract:
<jats:p>We benchmark four multi-agent orchestration frameworks (plain-Python Blackboard, CrewAI, OpenAI Swarm, LangGraph) on a shared audit-judgement task: four AI agents embodying canonical audit personas (Engagement Partner, Audit Senior, Skeptic Reviewer, Independence Checker) must each form an audit opinion on four real-world corporate scandals (Enron 2001, Wirecard 2020, SVB 2023, Tesco 2014), using only the public information available before each scandal broke. Each framework's output is scored against hidden ground truth on four axesjudgement accuracy, evidence rigour (red-flag recall), reasoning quality (LLM-judged), and calibration-plus a manual framework-ergonomics axis.&nbsp;
<div>
 The lowest-abstraction framework (plain Python with a Blackboard pattern) outperformed the three production frameworks (15.33 vs 13.84, 12.94, 5.00 out of 20 on auto-scored axes). We initially hypothesised the differentiator was a forced verdict gate-an independence-checker node that rejects unsupported opinions and forces rework. A deconfounding experiment adding the gate to LangGraph did not confirm this: the gated variant (12.64-13.01) did not recover plain_python's score, ruling out the gate as the sole driver and leaving the Blackboard's input-digest reactivity as the leading alternative explanation. Evidence-surfacing and opinion-formation emerged as decoupled capabilities: the framework with the highest red-flag recall (Swarm, 4.44/5, including 100% on one case) had the lowest judgement accuracy (1.50/5) and refused to commit to any verdict. Agents were systematically over-cautious relative to the real auditors who failed (0 of 16 runs issued a "Clean" opinion; the real auditors issued Clean on all four), and mostly correctly so given the evidence constraint. The paper was independently peer-reviewed by a second LangGraph multi-agent system (three reviewer personas + editor, with a conditional reconsideration loop); the peer review correctly identified the gate-framework confound that the deconfounding experiment confirmed. We discuss implications for multi-agent framework design, LLM-as-auditor research, and the audit profession's structural under-caution problem.
</div></jats:p>

records.title: Lightweight Edge AI framework for Real Time Air Quality Analysis
records.abstract: Recent developments in the field of machine learning and deep learning have led to the improvement of air quality monitoring and forecasting, which allows making more accurate, efficient, and scalable predictions.Most of the current solutions are based on large models that require significant computing capabilities or continuous connectivity with a cloud, which limits their use in resource-constrained environments. The model presented in this paper is a lightweight Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) that was trained on one year of historical data (365 days) of the Open-Meteo API and then connected to low-cost IoT sensors (PMS7003 to measure PM2.5/PM10 and DHT22 to measure temperature/humidity) on a microcontroller (ESP32). With the help of TensorFlow Lite (TFLite) to infer the model on-the-fly, the model demonstrates high performance with an R2 of 0.9402, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0367 and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.0424 and has minimal resource needs in relation to the more traditional methods. The proposed system provides a high level of efficiency and edge deployment practicable than traditional benchmarks and is most appropriate to mobile platforms and resource constrained platforms. The study offers a convenient, practical system of real time air quality intelligence in emerging economies.

records.title: Before the Algorithm: The BRAIF AI Readiness Framework for Indian PSUs, MSMEs and Statutory InstitutionsA Suggested Benchmark Approach for Determining AI Readiness, and for Structuring Responsible AI Selection and Engagement
records.abstract:
<jats:p><div>
 <p>Indian public sector undertakings (PSUs), micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and statutory institutions are under growing pressure to adopt artificial intelligence, yet most start from different positions and face different constraints. Many begin tools before they have decided what AI is for, who is accountable, where data may lawfully reside, how employees are already using unsanctioned tools, or what the whole programme will cost and return.&nbsp;&nbsp;<span>Others stall because the path to adoption is unclear.&nbsp;</span></p>
 <p>This paper proposes an AI Readiness Framework (BRAIF-AIR), a suggested benchmark approach for determining the AI readiness of these three organisational types and for turning the result into a pathway and a selection method. It comprises a Gate that profiles the organisation, and eleven readiness dimensions in four clusters (direction; assurance; foundations; capability and value), covering strategy and value, governance and policy, risk, legal compliance, data foundation, data residency and sovereignty, technology, security and shadow AI, people and culture, finance and return on investment, and ecosystem and procurement. The framework is operationalised through 87 indicators with entity-specific applicability, a five-level maturity scale tied to evidence, gating thresholds that apply a weakest-link rule rather than averaging, four readiness pathways, a use-case triage method, and an assessment protocol for consultants with integrity safeguards.&nbsp;</p>
 <p>A Responsible AI Audit Mechanism is integrated as the selection and engagement method that readiness unlocks, and the challenges identified are consolidated in a single register. The method combines a synthesis of readiness, maturity-model and public-sector AI literature with design-science construction; evaluation is proposed but not yet performed.&nbsp;</p>
 <p>The framework is deliberately not definitive: it is a nudge and a starting benchmark for researchers to test and extend and for consultants to adopt with care.</p>
</div>

records.title: Evidence Quality in Assurance-Oriented Benchmark Construction
records.abstract: Assurance studies built from public software incidents depend on evidence whose fitness for reconstruction and downstream assurance analysis is rarely characterized at the level of the semantic claims the analysis consumes. We study this evidence-quality problem in a frozen 40-case frame of public tool-using-agent and Model Context Protocol incidents, separating reconstructability, replay/source resolution, oracle feasibility, pairing, releaseability, and element-level provenance of authored assurance semantics. Reproducible-vulnerability benchmarks and vulnerability-data-quality studies already establish disclosure filtering and intrinsic data-quality assessment; our contribution is narrower and task-relative. Although 39/40 cases exposed a patch or corrected state, only 20/40 met the strict paired criteria. Among 15 prefix survivors that were not strict-eligible, nonexclusive blockers were reconstruction (14), releaseability (9), replay/source resolution (4), pairing (3), and oracle feasibility (1); C38 was technically reconstructable but excluded solely by Conditional releaseability. In a ten-case deep audit, 190 representation rows were provenance-classified, and all 52 analyzer-relevant semantic attributes were source-informed rather than independent ground truth. C4 showed conclusion-relevant uncertainty: unresolved enforcement activity produced different fixed-state conclusions under fail-open versus fail-closed assignments. We additionally release AIRR-40, a 40-case, 49-field registry with a 20-case exact-upstream strict manifest and reproducibility artifacts. The study does not estimate population readiness or detector accuracy; it characterizes evidence quality for assurance-oriented benchmark construction.

records.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Large language models (LLMs) show promise for clinical decision support, yet most validation studies evaluate single models, leaving questions about generalizability and vendor dependence unanswered. We assessed whether a standardized biomarker analysis framework maintains clinical-grade accuracy across multiple LLMs from independent providers.</jats:p>
                </jats:sec>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We developed a structured prompt-based framework for detecting eight clinical patterns (insulin resistance, diabetes, cardiovascular disease risk, chronic kidney disease risk, systemic inflammation, nutrient deficiency, liver risk, and anemia) from laboratory biomarkers. We evaluated five LLMs from four providers—Grok-3 (xAI), GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini (OpenAI), Claude Haiku 4.5 (Anthropic), and Gemini 2.0 Flash (Google)—using identical system prompts and inputs on 4,018 adults from the CDC NHANES 2017–2018. Ground truth was established using published clinical criteria (ADA, AHA, KDIGO, WHO). Performance was measured by F1 score with 95% confidence intervals, sensitivity, specificity, and positive predictive value.</jats:p>
                </jats:sec>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>All five models achieved clinical-grade performance (F1 > 0.86) on eight evaluable patterns. Mean F1 scores ranged from 0.865 (95% CI: 0.799–0.931) for GPT-4o-mini to 0.963 (95% CI: 0.930–0.996) for Grok-3. Flagship models significantly outperformed economy-tier models (mean F1: 0.940 vs 0.881; paired t-test p=0.004). Grok-3 achieved near-perfect scores on liver risk (F1=1.000), anemia (0.999), and nutrient deficiency (0.997). Cardiovascular disease risk was the most challenging pattern (F1 range: 0.853–0.885). JSON parse rates exceeded 99.9% for all models. Total benchmark cost was approximately $59 USD.</jats:p>
                </jats:sec>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>A standardized prompt-based framework achieves clinical-grade accuracy across five LLMs from four independent providers, demonstrating model-agnostic generalizability. These findings support the feasibility of vendor-independent clinical AI systems that can leverage multiple models without requiring framework revalidation.</jats:p>
                </jats:sec>

records.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid proliferation of highly capable, multimodal large language models (LLMs) throughout 2024 and 2025 has created a pivotal inflection point for the global workforce. This paper examines the emergent paradigm of human-AI collaboration, moving beyond the narrative of job displacement to a more nuanced analysis of task augmentation and skill evolution. We investigate the real-world integration of advanced AI assistants across key professional sectors-including creative industries, software development, and scientific research-to identify patterns of adoption and their impact on productivity, innovation, and an individual's sense of professional agency. Through a synthesis of recent case studies and labor market data, this analysis highlights the critical need for new training frameworks and organizational strategies that foster co-creativity between humans and AI. The findings suggest that enterprises prioritizing "AI literacy" and the redesign of workflows to leverage machine-generated insights are gaining a significant competitive advantage. This paper concludes with forwardlooking recommendations for educators, policymakers, and business leaders on cultivating a resilient and adaptive workforce prepared for a future where professional success is defined by the ability to effectively partner with intelligent systems.</jats:p>

records.title: Explainable and Prescriptive AI for Cyber-Physical NVH Quality Control in Smart Manufacturing: A Critical Review and Research Framework
records.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to predict noise, vibration, and harshness (NVH), detect faults, and identify quality deviations in rotating machinery and smart manufacturing. Yet high predictive accuracy does not answer the engineering questions required for process improvement: which manufacturing or geometric variable generated the response, whether the relationship is causal, what controllable setting should change, whether the change is physically and technologically feasible, and whether the intervention improves the measured product. This critical review integrates five evidence streams: direct gear and drivetrain NVH studies; explainable rotating-machinery diagnosis; explainable manufacturing-quality prediction; causal, counterfactual, and recourse methods; and digital-twin or closed-loop industrial control. The literature shows strong progress in feature attribution, saliency analysis, physics-informed representation, and interpretable fault-state estimation, but direct gear/NVH studies remain concentrated at prediction and explanation levels. To separate algorithmic sophistication from demonstrated engineering capability, we propose a cumulative Level 0–6 maturity framework spanning prediction, global explanation, local explanation, engineering root cause, actionable recommendation, physics-constrained prescription, and closed-loop validation. The framework supports comparison of studies and design of cyber-physical NVH quality-control systems that progress from explanation to traceable, feasible, and experimentally validated manufacturing action.</jats:p>

OpenEMR-AI: An Open-Source Ambient AI Scribe Framework, Benchmark, and Blinded Physician Evaluation (Preprint)
records.abstract:
BACKGROUND

Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes are being deployed at scale, with randomized trials demonstrating reductions in documentation time and burnout indicators. However, two gaps limit equitable adoption and rigorous validation. First, current deployments depend almost entirely on proprietary infrastructure, placing ambient documentation out of practical reach for federally qualified health centers (FQHCs), critical-access hospitals, and low- and middle-income country (LMIC) health systems. Second, automated evaluation of ambient-generated notes relies heavily on embedding-based similarity metrics whose agreement with clinician judgment on full clinical documentation has not been rigorously quantified.

 OBJECTIVE

To develop and release an open-source, vendor-independent ambient clinical documentation framework integrated with the open-source OpenEMR electronic health record (EHR) via SMART on FHIR (SoF), and to quantify divergence between widely used automated metrics and blinded physician judgment of full clinical documentation.

 METHODS

We deployed a multi-tenant serverless SMART-on-FHIR application that writes FHIR R4 resources back to OpenEMR. We benchmarked 13 ASR models on 335 conversational clinical recordings and 380 short-form utterances across four datasets, and seven open-weight LLMs for retrieval-augmented clinical note generation grounded on 1,000 disease-specific MIMIC-IV schemas. Four top-performing LLMs generated 160 summaries for 40 Fareez OSCE conversations paired with OpenEMR patient records. Three board-eligible physician fellows produced 480 blinded ratings on six PDQI-9/QNOTE dimensions. Inter-rater reliability used Gwet’s AC2 with ordinal weights. Model differences used Friedman tests with Bonferroni-corrected post-hoc Wilcoxon signed-rank tests; Kendall’s W was reported with 95% percentile-bootstrap confidence intervals from 10,000 conversation-block resamples.

 RESULTS

BERTScore F1 was virtually identical across the four clinician-evaluated models (0.800-0.803), yet clinician composite scores spanned 2.95-3.74 with significant model differences (p ≤ 0.002 for completeness, organization, conciseness, clinical utility, and overall quality). MedCAT UMLS-linked entity recall, but not embedding-based metrics, showed clinically meaningful separation that distinguished the medically tuned 4B model (composite 2.95) from the three larger general-purpose models (3.61-3.74). Voxtral Mini 3B led on institutional and Fareez OSCE recordings; medical-dictation ASR failed catastrophically. Per-encounter cost was approximately $0.02, a 98-99% reduction relative to commercial alternatives. Two persistent LLM failure modes of chart-overreach (≈22% of clinician comments, lower-bound estimate) and fabrication (≈21%) were intrinsic to current LLM behavior and require physician attestation.

 CONCLUSIONS

Embedding-based automated metrics systematically understate clinically meaningful quality differences that physicians detect in ambient-AI-generated notes; entity-based metrics partially recover these differences. Procurement, certification (FDA, CE), and post-market surveillance frameworks for ambient-AI scribes should require clinician-anchored and entity-based evaluation as primary endpoints, with embedding similarity reported only as supporting context. The complete SoF app, evaluation code, rater packets, and de-identified ratings are released open-source, lowering the access barrier for safety-net and resource-constrained settings.

EMSEIF Provides an Explainable AI Framework for Multi Stakeholder Curriculum Feedback and Quality Assurance in Higher Education
records.abstract: Higher education quality-assurance systems collect large volumes of curriculum feedback from students, teachers, alumni, parents and employers, yet the dominant institutional workflow still reduces these voices to descriptive percentages and post-hoc minutes. This study validates an Explainable Multi-Stakeholder Educational Intelligence Framework (EMSEIF) that converts real-world stakeholder feedback into aspect-level evidence, auditable recommendations and curriculum-improvement actions. The empirical setting is a 2023–24 structured curriculum feedback corpus from a participating higher education institution (HEI), represented by stakeholder forms, graphical analyses, action-taken letters and governance minutes. The system combines a curriculum aspect taxonomy, an educational knowledge graph, aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA), transformer-based multi-task classification, SHAP and Integrated Gradients explanations, subgroup fairness auditing and a human-in-the-loop (HITL) intervention engine. Validation uses stratified 5-fold cross-validation, ANOVA, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, confidence intervals, effect sizes, error analysis and ablation studies. Across stakeholder roles, the institutional evidence shows high but uneven satisfaction. Aerospace Engineering reported an overall impression distribution of 5.5% poor, 10.3% fair, 35.6% good, 30.4% very good and 18.2% excellent, while ECE showed 2.27% poor, 6.58% fair, 24.04% good, 36.66% very good and 30.43% excellent. EMSEIF improves macro-F1 over all classical and single-task transformer baselines and maps recurring concerns about practical exposure, internships, employability, AI/ML, ICT skills, communication, value-added courses and industry interaction into governance-ready recommendations. The principal contribution is not another conceptual AI-in-education framework. EMSEIF is positioned as an empirical educational intelligence system joining multi-stakeholder feedback, explainable NLP, curriculum knowledge graphs, statistical validation, fairness governance and action tracking. The result is a reproducible, institutionally deployable closed loop that moves from stakeholder voice to curriculum revision and measured improvement.

Why Generative AI Triumphs: A Conceptual Framework for Prediction Quality in AI Systems
Physics beats diffusion: Agentic AI-driven virtual screening benchmark on a GPCR target
records.abstract: Virtual screening (VS) campaigns require expert decisions at every stage, from active compound curation and decoy generation to receptor preparation, docking engine selection, and statistical evaluation. I show that an autonomous large language model (LLM) coding agent (Claude Code, Anthropic) can design and execute a complete VS benchmark pipeline without human coding intervention that requires only high-level scientific direction. The agent curated 1,000 FPR2 (a GPCR receptor) actives from ChEMBL (pChEMBL ≥ 5), generated ca. 10,000 property-matched decoys, prepared ligand libraries using two protocols (naive defaults and expert-guided), configured and ran docking with two fundamentally different engines; 1) Uni-Dock (GPU-accelerated physics-based) and 2) DiffDock (diffusion-based machine learning). Then it performed full statistical evaluation including ROC AUC, BEDROC, enrichment factors, DeLong tests, and paired bootstrap confidence intervals. Uni-Dock achieved ROC AUC = 0.70–0.73 with significant discrimination (permutation p < 0.0001), while DiffDock confidence scores yielded near-random performance (AUC = 0.54–0.56; Cliff’s d = negligible), consistent with its known underrepresentation of GPCR targets in training data. Expert-guided protocols improved Uni-Dock AUC by +0.020 (DeLong p = 0.003; paired bootstrap p = 0.002). Single-ligand redocking confirmed Vina reproduces the crystal pose (RMSD 0.22–0.39 Å) whereas both Uni-Dock batch mode (5.2–5.7 Å) and DiffDock (23–29 Å) failed. All code, data, and the agent’s skill file are openly available. Scientific contribution: This is the first demonstration of an LLM coding agent autonomously constructing a reproducible VS benchmark from scratch. The resulting benchmark provides the first head-to-head comparison of Uni-Dock and DiffDock on a GPCR target that reveals that physics-based docking (AUC = 0.70–0.73) substantially outperforms diffusion-based ML docking (AUC = 0.54–0.56, near-random) for this underrepresented target class.

records.title: MSR88 ASSESSING AI AND ML TOOL PERFORMANCE IN SLRS: A TARGETED LITERATURE REVIEW AND PERFORMANCE BENCHMARK FRAMEWORK
Measuring the Quality of AI-Generated Clinical Notes: A Systematic Review and Experimental Benchmark of Evaluation Methods
records.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>High-quality clinical documentation is essential for safe, effective care, yet producing it is time consuming and error prone. Large language models (LLMs) can assist with note generation, but clinical adoption is determined by the resulting note quality. However current evaluation practices vary, and their clinical relevance is unclear. Drawing on a multidisciplinary perspective, we examined how quality is assessed and how those assessments align with clinical demands.</jats:p>
                </jats:sec>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We systematically searched Ovid Medline and Scopus on 10 April 2025 for peer-reviewed studies that used LLMs in generating clinical notes and included an evaluation of the quality of the resulting text. The screening followed PRISMA and the protocol was preregistered in PROSPERO. Data on metrics, and outcomes were synthesised narratively. Based on these findings, we designed an experimental setup to test the most common evaluation metrics and an LLM-as-evaluator, included for its scalability across large test sets. The experiment used synthetic cases with targeted perturbations.</jats:p>
                </jats:sec>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Thirty-seven studies were included. The reporting was dominated by lexical overlap metrics, chiefly ROUGE and BLEU. Semantic similarity metrics, such as BERTScore and BLEURT, were less common. A human evaluation was frequent but heterogeneous, with criteria and methods defined using varying degrees of detail; the most common foci were correctness, fluency, and aspects of clinical acceptability. In our experimental setup, lexical overlap metrics detected deletions and modifications but penalised meaning-preserving paraphrases. Semantic metrics and LLM-as-evaluators were more tolerant of paraphrased perturbations, yet remained sensitive to relevant changes, with performance varying by model and language.</jats:p>
                </jats:sec>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Interpretation</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Current practice relies on lexical overlap metrics that are useful for cursory checks but insufficient as proxies for quality. We recommend a layered strategy that pairs semantic metrics with LLM-as-evaluator for scalability and includes targeted human adjudication. Broader, safety-focused validation across institutions and languages is needed before routine deployment.</jats:p>
                </jats:sec>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Funding</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Business Finland through the GenAID research project. Personal grants listed under Acknowledgments.</jats:p>
                </jats:sec>

HCCD-DS: A Reproducible Benchmark Dataset for Human--AI Decision Support Under Contextual Uncertainty
records.abstract: Decision support pipelines increasingly combine machine learning predictions with human judgment, yet most public benchmarks evaluate model outputs only and do not encode the interaction process that determines final decisions. This limits reproducible analysis of when human intervention improves or degrades system-level performance.We introduce HCCD-DS, a reproducible benchmark dataset that models decision-time interaction between an AI recommender and users with different expertise levels under contextual uncertainty. Each decision instance links input context, system confidence, explainability metadata, human acceptance/override behavior, override rationale, and realized outcome. The dataset covers healthcare, cybersecurity, and Internet of Things (IoT) scenarios to support cross-domain evaluation.Empirical analyses and benchmark experiments show that human intervention is condition-dependent: expert overrides are more likely to improve outcomes, while novice overrides more often reduce success. In addition, human action variables are substantially more predictable than final outcomes, indicating a plausible gap between behavioral predictability and outcome uncertainty. By exposing this structure in a unified and reusable resource, HCCD-DS supports method development for human-aware decision support, trust calibration, and explanation-aware interaction policies.

Benchmark Evaluation of the WordBinary AI-Text Detection Model on 9,000 AI-Generated Texts and 2,000 Pre-2015 Human Academic-Paper Samples
records.abstract: The growing use of large language models has increased demand for systems capable of distinguishing AI-generated text from genuine human writing. Such systems must achieve high sensitivity to machine-generated content while maintaining a sufficiently low false-positive rate to protect human authors. This study evaluated the WordBinary AI-text detection model using 11,000 labelled text samples: 9,000 AI-generated samples and 2,000 samples obtained from pre-2015 human academic papers. The AI corpus included normal and humanised outputs associated with Claude, Cohere, DeepSeek, Gemini, Mistral, OpenAI and OpenRouter platform groups. The human corpus contained 400 samples from each of five academic disciplines: computer science, economics, statistics, physics and mathematics. The model classified all 9,000 AI-generated samples as AI and all 2,000 human academic samples as human. The resulting confusion matrix contained 9,000 true positives, 2,000 true negatives, no false negatives and no false positives. Observed sensitivity, specificity, precision, negative predictive value, F1 score, balanced accuracy and overall accuracy were therefore all 100%. Exact 95% binomial confidence intervals were 99.959% to 100% for sensitivity, 99.816% to 100% for specificity and 99.966% to 100% for overall accuracy. The one-sided implication of observing no false positives in 2,000 human samples is that the 95% upper confidence bound for the underlying false-positive rate is approximately 0.184%, subject to the assumption that observations were statistically independent. Platform-level mean AI scores ranged from 98.56% for DeepSeek-associated outputs to 99.98% for OpenAI-associated outputs. All normal and humanised AI groups achieved 100% observed recall. The highest AI score among the human academic samples was 1.07%, while approximate domain-level mean scores ranged from 0.01% to 0.31%. The results demonstrate complete classification of the supplied test set. They do not, however, establish universal 100% accuracy. Independent external validation, documentation of the decision threshold, control for training-test contamination, clustered statistical analysis, multilingual testing and evaluation on mixed-authorship and AI-polished documents are required before broader generalisation.

records.title: RNA3D-Decoy: A Large-Scale Benchmark Dataset of AI-Generated RNA Structure Models for Quality Assessment
records.abstract:
<jats:p>
                  Recent advances in AI-based RNA structure prediction have increased the availability of candidate models, but their accuracy remains variable. Developing reliable quality assessment (QA) methods requires datasets that represent contemporary prediction errors across diverse targets and molecular contexts. Here, we present RNA3D-Decoy, a large-scale bench-mark dataset comprising 103,549 decoys for 677 experimentally determined targets, including 416 RNA-only structures, 117 RNA structures with metal ions, and 144 RNA-protein complexes. Decoys were generated using five biomolecular predictors: AlphaFold 3, ESMFold2, Protenix, Chai-1, and Boltz-2. Each decoy is evaluated against its experimental reference using TM-score, lDDT, and RMSD, with global and local quality annotations where applicable. DockQ scores additionally characterize RNA-protein interface quality. Target grouping incorporates both RNA and protein sequence relationships to support dataset partitioning. Analyses reveal distinct quality distributions across dataset levels and target-dependent differences among predictors, with each predictor contributing the highest-TM-score model for a subset of targets. Broad pooled score distributions also coexist with limited within-target score variation, particularly for RNA-protein complexes, emphasizing the importance of target-level characterization. By combining AI-generated decoys, standardized quality labels, and structured metadata, RNA3D-Decoy provides a resource for developing and evaluating methods for global quality estimation, local error prediction, and candidate-model ranking. records.title: A Dual-Branch Explainable AI Framework Combining Machine and Deep Learning for Air Quality Forecasting in Indian Cities
records.abstract: A precise Air Quality Index (AQI) forecasting is essential for ecosystem monitoring and societal health management. This study proposes a dual-branch explainable AI framework that brings together machine learning models (XGBoost, LightGBM,CatBoost, Linear Regression) and deep learning models (LSTM, GRU, TCN, Transformer) for AQI prediction across major Indian cities. Comprehensive preprocessing, including temporal feature extraction and rolling mean engineering, was applied to ensure high-quality and reliable inputs. The GRU model achieved the best performance with an R2 score of 0.9886 and an RMSE of 0.0032. A multi-level XAI analysis was incorporated, using Feature Importance for machine learning models and Integrated Gradients, Perturbation Sensitivity, Feature Occlusion, and Temporal Receptive Field Profiling for deep learning models. The results consistently identified AQI_7d_avg and AQI_30d_avg as the most influential predictors. The proposed framework combines strong predictive accuracy with transparent interpretability, supporting data-driven environmental policymaking and sustainable air pollution control system across Indian cities.

records.title: ProSocial AI as a Catalyst of Quality of Life: A Multilevel Framework for Pro-People, Pro-Planet, and Pro-Potential Futures
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly mediates how people learn, work, seek care, form relationships, access public services, and respond to environmental risk. Its quality-of-life effects extend beyond technical performance and economic productivity. This conceptual article develops the ProSocial AI-Quality of Life Catalyst Model (PAI-QOL), a multilevel framework explaining when and how AI can contribute to futures that are pro-people, pro-planet, and pro-potential. ProSocial AI is defined as AI deliberately designed, deployed, and governed to generate demonstrable and fairly distributed gains in multidimensional quality of life, strengthen human and collective capabilities, and protect the ecological conditions of future well-being. A problem-driven integrative synthesis identifies four conversion pathways: agency and capability, relational and social-capital, institutional and public-value, and regenerative and intergenerational. Their benefits depend on four enabling conditions: Double Literacy, meaningful participation, contestability, and proportionality. The model connects the 4T architecture of tailored, trained, tested, and targeted AI with a 4 x 4 lens spanning aspirations, emotions, thoughts, and sensations across individual, community and institutional, national and systemic, and planetary and intergenerational levels. Four propositions translate the framework into testable claims. A multidimensional measurement strategy distinguishes genuine prosocial contribution from intention, compliance, or branding. ProSocial AI emerges as a disciplined direction for innovation that expands agency, reinforces trustworthy relationships and institutions, preserves future capability, and produces social value within planetary limits.

records.title: A Benchmark Framework for Trajectory Vectorization in Unsupervised Settings
records.abstract: The growth of location-tracking technologies has generated large spatiotemporal datasets that require efficient analysis methods. Recent approaches focus on vectorizing the data as a preprocessing step to enable the application of off-the-shelf classical machine learning techniques. To date, such approaches have primarily been evaluated in supervised tasks. This paper presents a benchmark framework for assessing these methods in unsupervised settings, where no target labels are available. We extend and systematically evaluate five families of vectorization techniques: feature-based, shapelet-based, dictionary-based, matrix-based, and deep-learning-based, on a suite of synthetic and real-world datasets. The framework assesses both clustering quality and cross-vectorization diversity through quantitative and qualitative analyses. Overall, the findings demonstrate that these vectorization approaches offer a valuable option for unsupervised trajectory analysis. Additionally, our paper provides insight into which vectorization technique is most suitable for the specific characteristics of the task under analysis. For example, our findings indicate that feature-based approaches are most effective for capturing motion dynamics, while shapelet-based methods excel at identifying localized geometric patterns.

QNLP-Bench: A Standardized Benchmark and Evaluation Framework for Quantum Natural Language Processing
records.abstract: Quantum Natural Language Processing (QNLP) seeks to combine com positional models of meaning with quantum and quantum-inspired computational frameworks. While recent work has demonstrated the feasibility of implement ing such models, empirical results remain difficult to compare due to heteroge neous evaluation practices, weak or mismatched baselines, and limited reporting of computational resources. As a result, it is often unclear when compositional or quantum-inspired approaches are genuinely warranted. In this work, we introduce QNLP-Bench, a standardized benchmark and evalu ation framework designed to enable fair, reproducible, and compute-aware assess ment of QNLP models. The benchmark defines shared task specifications, fixed preprocessing pipelines, capacity-matched classical baselines, and explicit resource reporting requirements across classical, quantum-inspired, and quantum models. Rather than targeting claims of quantum advantage, QNLP-Bench aims to clar ify the empirical conditions under which compositional structure contributes to improved generalization. We provide a minimal but diagnostic experimental instantiation of the bench mark using controlled sentence classification tasks that separate lexically driven and role-sensitive regimes. The results demonstrate that simple baselines suffice on lexically separable tasks, while explicit encoding of grammatical structure is nec essary for success on role-dependent problems, albeit at increased computational cost. These findings illustrate the value of standardized, diagnostic benchmarks for grounding progress in QNLP and for guiding future research toward transparent and principled evaluation practices

records.title: From Data Quality to AI-Native Operating Models: A Practitioner Framework for Enterprise AI Capability Coherence
records.abstract: <jats:p>Enterprise artificial intelligence is often seen in the context of the capability of the models used, data availability, technology infrastructure, or responsible AI governance. But organizations might have all these things but still face challenges in scaling their AI in the business processes. The argument presented in this paper is that the problem is both organizational and technical. The success of enterprise AI requires a coherent set of capabilities covering data quality, data governance, data products, data contracts, AI platform, accountability, lineage, explainability, ownership, value measurement, and operating model. The main proposition developed in this paper is that capability coherence is essential for scaling enterprise AI. The paper explores the proposition via conceptual synthesis of 12 practitioner essays published between July and September 2026 on the topics including data quality and governance, data products, AI ecosystems, responsible AI, decision traceability, data ownership, governance value, and AI-native operating models. The practitioner corpus is considered together with existing research and institutional literature, including BCBS 239, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, data-mesh research, IT governance, and dynamic capabilities theory.</jats:p>

records.title: VQD-CTS Prediction Model: An AI-Driven Framework for Predicting Cost-to-Serve Using Engineering Velocity, Quality, and Developer Experience
records.abstract: Modern software engineering organizations leverage multi-dimensional perfor mance indicators—Velocity, Quality, and Developer Experience (DX)—to gauge delivery health. However, establishing a quantifiable link between these engineer ing signals and financial outcomes like Cost-to-Serve (CTS) remains a significant challenge. This paper proposes the VQD-CTS Prediction Model, a comprehensive machine learning framework designed to predict CTS using a synthesis of V-Q-D metrics. Our ensemble regression model, trained on extensive synthetic enter prise data, achieved an R2 score of 0.885 with MAE of 79.93. Feature importance analysis identified code complexity, defect density, cycle time, and infrastructure cost share as dominant predictors. This framework supports organizations a scal able, data-driven approach to forecast budgetary needs and optimize engineering investments.

records.title: A Biomedical Benchmark and Modular RAG Framework for Text2Cypher
records.abstract: Background Biomedical Knowledge Graphs (bioKGs) are increasingly used to integrate heterogeneous biomedical data, including genomic interactions, disease associations, and drug–target relationships. Property graph databases, such as Neo4j, provide an effective framework for representing and querying these data through the Cypher query language. However, writing Cypher queries requires substantial technical expertise, limiting the accessibility of bioKGs to domain experts. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently shown promise for translating natural language (NL) questions into Cypher queries, progress in the biomedical domain remains constrained by the limited availability of representative benchmarks and reproducible evaluation frameworks. Results We present bio2C, a FAIR-compliant biomedical benchmark comprising 2,500 curated NL-Cypher pairs covering diverse biomedical information needs, graph schemas, and progressively more expressive Cypher constructs. Building upon this resource, we introduce a modular Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework that systematically combines graph schema descriptions, retrieved NL-Cypher examples, and query execution outputs, thereby establishing reproducible baselines for future Text2Cypher research. We evaluate the resulting pipelines using both proprietary (GPT) and open-source (LLaMA) LLMs together with their fine-tuned counterparts. Experimental results show that retrieving representative NL-Cypher examples consistently outperforms schema-based prompting, with particularly pronounced improvements for fine-tuned models. The best-performing configuration improves execution accuracy by 31.6 percentage points over current schema-based prompting strategies. Conclusions This work provides two complementary resources for biomed-ical Text2Cypher research: a high-quality FAIR benchmark and a modular evaluation framework for systematically studying retrieval-augmented prompting strategies. Together, they establish reproducible baselines for developing and comparing future Text2Cypher systems while demonstrating that carefully curated benchmarks and representative retrieval examples substantially improve Cypher generation over bioKGs. The benchmark, source code, and evaluated pipelines are publicly available through Zenodo and GitHub.
